key_points.point: The document acknowledges that institutions are competing to build ever-larger language models, which is a key driver of progress in the field.
key_points.verbatim: BERT, its variants, GPT-2/3, and others, most recently Switch-C, have pushed the boundaries of the possible both through architectural innovations and through sheer size.

key_points.point: The document notes that increasing model size and training data has consistently led to performance improvements across a wide array of tasks.
key_points.verbatim: Using these pretrained models and the methodology of fine-tuning them for specific tasks, researchers have extended the state of the art on a wide array of tasks as measured by leaderboards on specific benchmarks for English.

key_points.point: The document acknowledges that AI research is a valuable resource that should be directed toward building a technological ecosystem where benefits are evenly distributed or accrue to marginalized groups.
key_points.verbatim: our research time and effort a valuable resource, to be spent to the extent possible on research projects that build towards a technological ecosystem whose benefits are at least evenly distributed or better accrue to those historically most marginalized.

key_points.point: The document suggests that researchers should incorporate energy and compute efficiency into model evaluations to prevent economic inequities.
key_points.verbatim: The resources needed to train and tune state-of-the-art models stand to increase economic inequities unless researchers incorporate energy and compute efficiency in their model evaluations.

key_points.point: The document advocates for a shift in research goals from simply making models bigger to understanding how machines achieve tasks and form part of socio-technical systems.
key_points.verbatim: we believe there is more to be gained by focusing on understanding how machines are achieving the tasks in question and how they will form part of socio-technical systems.

key_points.point: The authors argue that the rapid development of ever-larger language models poses significant, under-examined risks that require urgent mitigation strategies.
key_points.verbatim: While investigating properties of LMs and how they change with size holds scientific interest, and large LMs have shown improvements on various tasks (§2), we ask whether enough thought has been put into the potential risks associated with developing them and strategies to mitigate these risks.

key_points.point: The authors highlight that large, uncurated datasets from the internet encode hegemonic viewpoints and biases that can cause real-world harm to marginalized populations.
key_points.verbatim: In §4, we discuss how large datasets based on texts from the Internet overrepresent hegemonic viewpoints and encode biases potentially damaging to marginalized populations.

key_points.point: The authors advocate for budgeting for dataset curation and documentation at the start of projects to avoid 'documentation debt' and mitigate risks.
key_points.verbatim: We recommend mitigating these risks by budgeting for curation and documentation at the start of a project and only creating datasets as large as can be sufficiently documented.

key_points.point: The authors argue that language models do not perform natural language understanding and that their success is limited to manipulating linguistic form, which can mislead the public about their true capabilities.
key_points.verbatim: As we discuss in §5, LMs are not performing natural language understanding, and only have success in tasks that can be approached by manipulating linguistic form [14].

key_points.point: The document emphasizes the need for careful planning and documentation of data and model uses before building systems to mitigate risks and harms.
key_points.verbatim: In order to mitigate the risks that come with the creation of increasingly large LMs, we urge researchers to shift to a mindset of careful planning, along many dimensions, before starting to build either datasets or systems trained on datasets.

key_points.point: The document advocates for thorough documentation of data selection and collection processes to identify potential risks and stakeholders who might be negatively impacted.
key_points.verbatim: This documentation should reflect and indicate researchers’ goals, values, and motivations in assembling data and creating a given model. It should also make note of potential users and stakeholders, particularly those that stand to be negatively impacted by model errors or misuse.

key_points.point: The document suggests using pre-mortem analyses to reverse-engineer potential failures and risks before deploying new models.
key_points.verbatim: To that end, LM development may benefit from guided evaluation exercises such as pre-mortems [68]. Frequently used in business settings before the deployment of new products or projects, pre-mortem analyses center hypothetical failures and ask team members to reverse engineer previously unanticipated causes.

key_points.point: The document advocates for value sensitive design methodologies to identify stakeholders and ensure systems support their values, helping to identify harms early.
key_points.verbatim: Value sensitive design [49, 50] provides a range of methodologies for identifying stakeholders... working with them to identify their values, and designing systems that support those values.

key_points.point: The authors emphasize that large language models encode and amplify hegemonic biases, which disproportionately harm marginalized communities.
key_points.verbatim: In the case of US and UK English, this means that white supremacist and misogynistic, ageist, etc. views are overrepresented in the training data, not only exceeding their prevalence in the general population but also setting up models trained on these datasets to further amplify biases and harms.

key_points.point: The authors highlight the significant environmental and financial costs of training large language models, noting that these costs disproportionately impact marginalized communities.
key_points.verbatim: As we outline in §3, increasing the environmental and financial costs of these models doubly punishes marginalized communities that are least likely to benefit from the progress achieved by large LMs and most likely to be harmed by negative environmental consequences of its resource consumption.

key_points.point: The authors argue that the current trend of building ever-larger models is driven by competition rather than careful consideration of societal impact or stakeholder values.
key_points.verbatim: BERT, its variants, GPT-2/3, and others, most recently Switch-C, have pushed the boundaries of the possible both through architectural innovations and through sheer size. ... we ask whether enough thought has been put into the potential risks associated with developing them and strategies to mitigate these risks.

key_points.point: The document argues that simply increasing dataset size is not a viable strategy for inclusivity and that feeding AI systems the world's 'ugliness' will result in the AI reflecting those harms.
key_points.verbatim: As discussed in §4.1, simply turning to massive dataset size as a strategy for being inclusive of diverse viewpoints is doomed to failure. We recall again Birhane and Prabhu’s [18] words (inspired by Ruha Benjamin [15]): “Feeding AI systems on the world’s beauty, ugliness, and cruelty, but expecting it to reflect only the beauty is a fantasy.”

key_points.point: The document highlights the environmental and financial costs of large models, noting that these costs are often borne by those who do not benefit from the technology.
key_points.verbatim: We have identified a wide variety of costs and risks associated with the rush for ever larger LMs, including: environmental costs (borne typically by those not benefiting from the resulting technology); financial costs, which in turn erect barriers to entry...

key_points.point: The document warns that synthetic text generated by LMs can enter conversations without any entity being accountable for truthfulness or meaning.
key_points.verbatim: We note that the risks associated with synthetic but seemingly coherent text are deeply connected to the fact that such synthetic text can enter into conversations without any person or entity being accountable for it.

factual_claims.claim: Training large language models requires significant energy, often comparable to trans-American flights, and contributes to carbon emissions.
Large language models trained on internet data encode hegemonic viewpoints and biases that can harm marginalized populations.
Language models do not perform natural language understanding but instead manipulate linguistic form based on statistical patterns.
Training and tuning state-of-the-art models requires significant financial and environmental resources, which can exacerbate economic inequities.
Large language models can memorize training data, leading to risks of data leakage.
Synthetic text generated by language models can enter conversations without any entity being accountable for its truthfulness.

unmapped_concepts.concept: The authors argue that collecting ever-larger datasets without budgeting for curation and documentation at the start of a project leads to 'documentation debt,' which perpetuates harm without recourse.

unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: A stochastic parrot is a system that generates fluent, seemingly coherent text by statistically stitching together sequences of linguistic forms observed in training data, without any reference to meaning or communicative intent.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The authors define a language model as a 'stochastic parrot' because it haphazardly stitches together sequences of linguistic forms based on probabilistic information without any reference to meaning.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This is the core metaphor of the document and a fundamental concept for understanding the authors' critique of language models.
unmapped_concepts.Accelerationist Interpretation: Accelerationists might argue that even if models are 'stochastic parrots,' their ability to manipulate linguistic form is sufficient to deliver immense practical value and productivity gains.
unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: Safetyists would emphasize that the 'stochastic parrot' nature of these models makes them inherently unpredictable and prone to generating harmful, biased, or nonsensical content that can be mistaken for meaningful communication.
unmapped_concepts.Skeptic Interpretation: Skeptics would use the 'stochastic parrot' concept to debunk the hype around AI intelligence, arguing that these models are just pattern-matchers and should not be trusted with important decisions.
